items.title: Austria Sets Out Drone Defence Plan
items.gist: The government has presented a new plan to strengthen Austria’s protection against drones.
items.summary: Austria presented a drone-defence strategy on Tuesday. Chancellor Christian Stocker attended the presentation by the Cobra police unit and the armed forces. The plan aims to improve the country’s ability to detect and respond to drones. Drones can threaten public safety and important infrastructure. The announcement comes as European countries pay closer attention to security risks. The report describes the strategy’s presentation but does not give all its details.
items.host_open: A new security plan is on the table, and drones are part of the debate. How does that look from Austria?

items.title: A1 Plans 430 Net Job Cuts
items.gist: Telecom company A1 says it plans to reduce its Austrian workforce next year.
items.summary: A1 Austria plans a net reduction of 430 jobs in 2027. The company expects about 500 departures and 70 new hires in growing areas. It currently employs just under 6,000 people in Austria. A1 says it wants to cut costs by €300 million by 2030. The company also plans to invest up to €500 million a year in Austria. The announcement raises questions about workers’ futures as the company changes its business.
items.host_open: A1 is cutting some roles while hiring for others. How do you feel about that?

items.title: Ukraine Strike Kills Libyan Officers
items.gist: Two Libyan naval officers have died after a Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian warship in Libya.
items.summary: Two Libyan naval officers died from injuries after a Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian warship in Libya. The attack took place far from Ukraine’s front lines. Libya’s army has vowed to retaliate, according to the report. The incident adds a dangerous new dimension to the war between Russia and Ukraine. The attack’s consequences for people in Libya and the wider region remain uncertain. The report describes the deaths and the army’s response; it does not establish what retaliation will involve.
items.host_open: The fighting has brought tragedy to Libya. How do you feel about its widening reach?

items.title: Amnesty Seeks Tigray War Crimes Probe
items.gist: Amnesty International is calling for an independent investigation into shelling in Ethiopia’s Tigray region.
items.summary: Amnesty International says shelling of civilian areas in Tigray should be investigated as possible war crimes. Residents near the Eritrean border have described military build-ups and fear of renewed fighting. The report attributes the shelling to Ethiopian forces and an allied militia. Fighting resumed in September, after a 2022 agreement ended a two-year war. Amnesty is calling for an independent inquiry; the allegations have not been decided by a court. The renewed tension matters to civilians in Tigray and neighbouring areas.
items.host_open: For people in Tigray, renewed fighting brings real fear. How does this report make you feel?

items.title: Canary Islands See Record Migrant Arrivals
items.gist: Nearly 2,000 people reached Spain’s Canary Islands in a single day, an unusually high number.
items.summary: Nearly 2,000 people arrived in the Canary Islands in one day, setting a single-day record. The islands are a key entry point for migrants trying to reach Europe. More than 26,000 people have reached them this year, according to the report. About half of this year’s arrivals came in November. The increase puts pressure on local services and renews debate about migration policy. The report gives arrival figures but does not set out the views of migrants or Spanish officials in detail.
items.host_open: That is a striking number of arrivals in one day. Did that surprise you?

items.title: Kimmel Jokes About Trump and Nvidia
items.gist: Kimmel’s recent monologue touched on Trump, Nvidia and the company’s leadership turmoil.
items.summary: Jimmy Kimmel’s November 23 monologue covered President Donald Trump and Nvidia. The company has recently faced a leadership crisis, including the departure of its chief executive, Jensen Huang. Kimmel also addressed Trump’s comments about the company and its role in technology and national security. The monologue used the subject for political satire. This rundown reports the underlying news topic, not the jokes. The show’s segment does not establish the disputed claims about the company.
items.host_open: Washington and Silicon Valley are tangled up in this story. Did that surprise you?

items.title: EU Academy Warns of Data Leak
items.gist: The European Commission has warned users of its EU Academy platform about a data leak after a cyberattack.
items.summary: The European Commission warned users of its EU Academy platform about a data leak. The warning followed a cyberattack driven by artificial intelligence, according to the report. The platform provides learning resources connected to the European Union. A data leak can expose personal information and weaken trust in online services. The report does not specify how many users were affected or what information was exposed. The Commission’s warning signals that users should take the incident seriously while details are assessed.
items.host_open: Even a learning platform can become a target online. How do you feel about that?

items.title: Athens Museum Reopens After Restoration
items.gist: Greece’s oldest modern-era museum has reopened on the Acropolis after major restoration work.
items.summary: Greece’s oldest modern-era museum has reopened on the Acropolis in Athens. It had been closed for a major restoration. The reopening gives visitors access to a refreshed cultural site in one of Greece’s most important historic areas. The museum’s return is also a boost for local tourism and cultural life. The report describes the reopening but does not give details about every part of the restoration. Visitors can once again explore the museum and its collection.
items.host_open: Athens has welcomed an old museum back to life. What do you enjoy most about visiting museums?
